formation.title: The Confederacy United
formation.text:
The five fires of the Haudenosaunee burn as one. From the eastern door of the Kanienkehaka to the western door of the Onondowaga, the nations have gathered beneath the Tree of Great Peace at Onondaga, where the Great Peacemaker Deganawida planted it generations ago. The fifty sachems of the Grand Council sit in their appointed places, the white roots of peace spreading in every direction.

But a confederacy must choose its path. Will we extend the roots of peace through diplomacy and council, binding other nations to our law? Or will we follow the war roads, our warriors carrying the name of the Longhouse to the edges of the world?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let the roots of peace extend to all nations.

modifiers.name: The Great Law of Peace
modifiers.text: The Kaianere'ko:wa binds the Five Nations beneath the Tree of Great Peace, its roots reaching in all directions. Disputes are resolved in council, not by war among ourselves. The strength of the Longhouse is unity.

options.text: The war roads shall carry our name far.

modifiers.name: War Road of the Longhouse
modifiers.text: The Haudenosaunee extend their reach along the war roads, their warriors ranging far to bring captives, furs, and tribute back to the Longhouse. What the council decides, the war parties enforce.

advances.name: Keepers of the Two Doors
advances.text: The league is one house lying east to west. The Mohawk keep its eastern door and the Seneca its western, and the Onondaga tend the fire in the middle. Word from abroad is received at a door and carried along the house to the council, so that no nation treats alone.

advances.name: Longhouse Governance
advances.text: The longhouse serves as both communal dwelling and political unit, where clan mothers select sachems and multiple families share resources under one roof.

advances.name: The War Captain's Feast
advances.text: A captain who means to go out gives a feast in his town and sings his war song, and those who take up the song go with him. No council orders a war party out and none can forbid it.

advances.name: Three Sisters Agriculture
advances.text: Corn, beans, and squash (the Three Sisters) are planted together in mounds, each plant supporting the others: corn provides stalks for beans to climb, beans fix nitrogen for corn, and squash shades the soil.

advances.name: Canoe Warfare
advances.text: Haudenosaunee war parties travel by bark canoe, sinking their vessels beneath rocks by day and paddling through the night to strike far from home before retreating.

advances.name: Palisade Fortification
advances.text: Haudenosaunee villages are surrounded by triple rows of sharpened stakes interlaced with bark, with platforms holding stones and water jars to repel attackers.

advances.name: Wampum Diplomacy
advances.text: Strings and belts of shell beads serve as diplomatic credentials, treaty records, and mnemonic devices, encoding agreements in patterns of purple and white.

advances.name: Forest Warrior Tactics
advances.text: Warriors trained in woodland combat fight from ambush among the trees, using their intimate knowledge of the terrain to outmaneuver larger forces.

advances.name: Clan Mother Authority
advances.text: The clan mothers hold the power to nominate and depose sachems, approve declarations of war, and distribute the harvest: the true political authority of the Longhouse.

advances.name: Condolence Ceremony
advances.text: When a sachem dies, the Condolence Ceremony clears the minds of the grieving, wipes their tears, and raises a new chief to fill the empty seat on the Grand Council.

advances.name: The Council Fire
advances.text: The central fire at Onondaga never goes out. Here the fifty sachems gather to debate matters affecting all the nations, their decisions binding the entire Confederacy.

advances.name: Fur Trade Network
advances.text: Haudenosaunee hunters and traders operate across a vast network stretching from the Atlantic coast to the Great Lakes, exchanging beaver pelts for European manufactured goods. Deer hides dressed in the longhouses go down the river with the beaver.

advances.name: Firearms Adoption
advances.text: Through trade with the Dutch at Fort Orange, Haudenosaunee warriors obtain muskets and learn to integrate them with traditional ambush and raiding tactics. A musket is of use only while it can be mended, and a smith is asked for in every town that treats with the newcomers.

advances.name: War Chief System
advances.text: Condoled war chiefs, raised through ceremony and proven in battle, lead disciplined retinues of experienced warriors on campaigns far beyond the Confederacy's borders.

advances.name: The Beaver Wars
advances.text: The Haudenosaunee wage a decades-long campaign to control the Great Lakes fur trade, shattering rival confederacies and establishing dominance over a vast territory. The small parties of the mourning war give way to armies of a thousand that winter in the enemy's country.

event.title: The Beaver Wars
event.text:
The fur trade has transformed the world of the Great Lakes. European traders hunger for beaver pelts, and the Haudenosaunee stand at the crossroads between the Dutch at Fort Orange and the vast hunting grounds of the interior. But our rivals (the Wendat, the Neutrals, the Erie) control the western beaver territories.

Since the 1640s, our warriors have carried muskets alongside their war clubs, striking deep into enemy territory with devastating effect. The Wendat Confederacy has been shattered, their survivors scattered. The Great Lakes lie open before us. But with dominance comes a choice: do we seize control of the trade routes by force, or do we establish ourselves as the indispensable middlemen, playing the Europeans against each other while we grow rich on the passage of furs?

options.text: We shall dominate the fur trade by force.

modifiers.name: Fur Trade Dominance
modifiers.text: Haudenosaunee warriors have shattered rival confederacies and seized control of the Great Lakes fur trade, channeling beaver pelts through their territory to European markets.

options.text: We shall be the brokers between all nations.

modifiers.name: Fur Trade Brokers
modifiers.text: Rather than monopolizing the trade by force alone, the Haudenosaunee have positioned themselves as indispensable intermediaries between European traders and the peoples of the interior.

advances.name: Two Row Wampum
advances.text: The Guswenta, two parallel rows of purple beads on a white field, represents two vessels traveling side by side, neither interfering with the other. This is the basis of Haudenosaunee sovereignty.

advances.name: Advanced Fortifications
advances.text: Haudenosaunee engineers incorporate European defensive concepts into traditional palisade designs, creating formidable village defenses with multiple walls and bastions.

advances.name: Towns of the Adopted
advances.text: After the Wendat and Neutral towns fell, whole villages came over together and were given land among the Seneca. Gandougarae was such a town: Wendat, Neutral and others who kept their own fields and in time were counted as Seneca.

advances.name: Lacrosse Tradition
advances.text: The Creator's Game (lacrosse) serves as both ceremonial contest and warrior training, with matches between villages sometimes involving hundreds of players in fierce athletic competition.

advances.name: The Covenant Chain
advances.text: A series of alliance agreements between the Haudenosaunee and the English Crown, symbolized by a silver chain of three links: Peace, Friendship, and Respect. Under the Chain the English keep smiths in the castles to stock and mend the guns they trade.

event.title: The Covenant Chain
event.text:
A silver chain has been forged between the Haudenosaunee and the English Crown: three links representing Peace, Friendship, and Respect. This Covenant Chain is no mere treaty but a living relationship, polished and renewed at regular councils where grievances are heard and gifts exchanged. Through the Chain, the Haudenosaunee speak for many nations, carrying the concerns of the western peoples to the English and receiving European trade goods in return.

The Chain gives us leverage no other native nation possesses. But leverage is a tool that cuts both ways. Do we bind ourselves more closely to the English alliance, gaining their weapons and trade, or do we maintain our independence, playing the English against the French as we have always done?

options.text: Polish the silver chain. Our alliance makes us strong.

modifiers.name: Silver Covenant Chain
modifiers.text: The polished chain of alliance with the English Crown gives the Haudenosaunee privileged access to trade goods, diplomatic recognition, and military cooperation.

options.text: We answer to no European king. Our independence is our strength.

modifiers.name: Sovereign Between Empires
modifiers.text: The Haudenosaunee maintain their independence by refusing permanent allegiance to any European power, using the threat of shifting alliance to extract concessions from both French and English.

advances.name: Musket Mastery
advances.text: Haudenosaunee warriors have fully adapted European firearms to their style of warfare, combining the musket's killing power with traditional mobility and forest-fighting skills.

advances.name: Tuscarora Adoption
advances.text: The Tuscarora, a related Iroquoian-speaking people driven from their Carolina homeland by colonial warfare, are adopted into the Confederacy as the Sixth Nation.

event.title: The Sixth Nation
event.text:
The Tuscarora have come from the south, refugees from a devastating war with the English colonists of Carolina. They speak a language akin to our own, and their suffering demands our response. The clan mothers have deliberated, and the Grand Council has agreed: the Tuscarora shall be adopted into the Confederacy under the protection of the Oneida, seated beside the younger brothers of the Longhouse.

From five fires, we become six. The Longhouse grows longer, its strength renewed by those who seek shelter beneath its rafters. This is the genius of the Confederacy: not conquest, but adoption. Not destruction, but incorporation. The tree has grown new roots.

advances.name: Wampum Trade Expansion
advances.text: Wampum production expands from ceremonial and diplomatic use to serve as a medium of exchange in the growing trade between native and European communities.

advances.name: Gantowisas
advances.text: The Gantowisas, women's councils, exercise decisive authority over matters of war and peace, food distribution, and the selection of leaders throughout the Confederacy.

advances.name: Balance of Power
advances.text: The Haudenosaunee exploit the rivalry between French and English colonies, shifting allegiance and playing one power against the other to extract maximum advantage.

advances.name: Controlled Burning
advances.text: Deliberate burning of undergrowth creates open parkland forests that improve hunting, facilitate travel, and enrich the soil for the next planting season.

advances.name: Grand Council Reforms
advances.text: The Grand Council adapts its procedures to address the challenges of a changing world, streamlining decision-making while preserving the consensus principle.

advances.name: Neutrality Policy
advances.text: Recognizing the dangers of choosing sides in European conflicts, the Grand Council adopts a policy of armed neutrality, refusing to commit the Confederacy to any permanent alliance.

advances.name: Military Adaptation
advances.text: Haudenosaunee warriors incorporate European military discipline alongside traditional tactics. The warriors of all the nations take the field together under their war chiefs, a force capable of both guerrilla warfare and set-piece engagements.

advances.name: Portage Control
advances.text: Control of the portage routes between the Great Lakes and the river systems gives the Haudenosaunee a stranglehold on the flow of goods between the interior and the coast. At each carrying place the nation that holds it carries the goods and canoes of all who pass, and is paid for it.

advances.name: Orenda
advances.text: Orenda, the spiritual power that flows through all living things, sustains the ceremonies and traditions that bind the Haudenosaunee together across the generations.

advances.name: The Four Kings in London
advances.text: In 1710 three Mohawk sachems and a Mahican were received by Queen Anne as the kings of the Five Nations. They asked for soldiers against Canada and for a fort and a chapel in the Mohawk country, and both were built. From then on Mohawk warriors and provincial rangers were raised to serve side by side.

advances.name: Mohawk in Print
advances.text: The Mohawk prayer book is printed again in London in 1787 with the Gospel of Mark in Joseph Brant's translation, and a schoolmaster teaches reading in Mohawk at the Grand River. The language of the eastern door is read as well as spoken.

advances.name: Buffalo Creek Council
advances.text: The Council at Buffalo Creek serves as the new diplomatic center of the Haudenosaunee, where the nations negotiate with the young American republic for the preservation of their lands and sovereignty.

advances.name: The Longhouse Religion
advances.text: Handsome Lake's Gaiwiio combines ancient Haudenosaunee ceremonies with new moral teachings, offering a path of cultural renewal in a time of crisis and dispossession. It is recited by the faithkeepers in longhouses raised for the purpose.

event.title: The Longhouse Religion
event.text:
Handsome Lake, a Seneca sachem who fell gravely ill, has received visions from the Creator. In his Code, he preaches against the evils that have crept into Haudenosaunee life since European contact: alcohol, witchcraft, domestic violence. But he also calls for a return to the ancient ceremonies, the Thanksgiving Address, the seasonal festivals that have sustained the People of the Longhouse since time immemorial.

The Longhouse Religion, as his followers call it, is neither purely traditional nor purely new. It adapts ancient practices to the realities of a changed world, offering the Haudenosaunee a path to cultural survival when the old ways seem under siege from every direction. From the ashes of despair, a spiritual fire has been rekindled.

options.text: The Creator's word shall guide us forward.

advances.name: Agricultural Modernization
advances.text: Haudenosaunee farmers adapt traditional polyculture methods to the demands of a market economy, selling surplus corn, beans, and squash to neighboring settlements. The plough is taken up in the fields, and flax is spun and woven on the farms.

advances.name: Cultural Preservation
advances.text: Through the dedicated efforts of keepers of tradition, the ceremonies, languages, and stories of the Haudenosaunee endure, ensuring that the Longhouse stands firm against the winds of change.

advances.name: Grand River Settlement
advances.text: The Six Nations settlement along the Grand River becomes a center of Haudenosaunee life, where the peoples rebuild their communities and maintain their confederate traditions.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Confederacy
destiny.text: The Haudenosaunee Confederacy has been forged anew. The Tree of Great Peace stands tall at Onondaga, and the fifty sachems of the Grand Council await the direction their people will take.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Confederacy's Path
event.text: The Haudenosaunee stand at a crossroads. The fifty sachems have gathered at the Council Fire, the nations united under one roof. The white roots of peace stretch in every direction, but the direction the Confederacy will grow depends on the decisions made in this council. Will the People of the Longhouse be remembered as masters of diplomacy, or as conquerors whose war roads reached the edges of the world?

destiny.name: Condolence Diplomacy
destiny.text: The condolence ceremony is carried beyond the Confederacy. The embassies go out, two peoples are taken under the Covenant Chain as dependants of the League, and wealth is gathered to fund the embassies across the northeast.

conditions.text: Chose The Great Law of Peace
Num subjects at least 2
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Condolence Reaches Further
event.text: What began as a ceremony to mourn the dead and raise new chiefs has become the foundation of a diplomatic tradition unlike any other. When the Haudenosaunee send condolence delegations to distant peoples, they carry not just words of comfort but an entire system of governance: the notion that grief can be transformed into political renewal, that mourning can build alliances stronger than any military pact. Nations that once feared the Longhouse now send their own delegations to Onondaga, eager to learn the arts of council and consensus.

options.text: We clear the minds of all who grieve.

destiny.name: The Silver Chain
destiny.text: Forge a diplomatic network spanning from Cataraqui on Lake Ontario to Shackamaxon on the Delaware. Control the trade crossroads that make the Haudenosaunee indispensable to every power in the region.

conditions.text: Own Cataraqui, or a subject owns it
Own Shackamaxon, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000

event.title: Polishing the Chain
event.text:
The diplomatic network has grown into something unprecedented: a web of alliances, trade agreements, and mutual obligations stretching across the northeast. The Silver Chain connecting the Haudenosaunee to the European powers and to other native confederacies must be constantly polished and renewed through councils, gift exchanges, and careful negotiation.

But there are two ways to tend such a chain. We can bind ourselves more closely to our partners, becoming the indispensable center of a great alliance system. Or we can maintain our independence, using the chain not to bind but to balance, playing each partner against the others while the Haudenosaunee grow wealthy on the tensions between them.

options.text: Bind the chain tighter. Alliance is strength.

modifiers.name: Polished Chain Alliance
modifiers.text: The Haudenosaunee have bound themselves tightly to their diplomatic partners, creating an alliance network that amplifies their influence at the cost of constant diplomatic maintenance.

options.text: We stand sovereign between all nations.

modifiers.name: Sovereign Mediators
modifiers.text: The Haudenosaunee maintain their independence between all factions, using their position as honest brokers to extract concessions from every side while answering to none.

destiny.name: The Extended Rafters
destiny.text: The rafters of the Longhouse are extended until peoples from the sea to the lakes sit under one roof. Shawmut on the eastern sea is held, and prestige and wealth are gathered. The House of the Wampum Keeper is raised to hold the belt of every nation taken in.

conditions.text: Own Shawmut, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Rafters Extended
event.text:
The Longhouse was built to be lengthened. Peoples who once sent war parties against it now ask for a place under its roof, and rafters are added for each: a seat at the fire, a name in the roll, a belt laid up at Onondaga to remember the day. From the eastern sea to the lakes the nations sit as props of one house.

So long a house may be kept in two ways. The league may raise council houses and belt houses in every country it has taken in, so that the roof is seen from afar. Or it may turn inward, and see that those now under the roof are fed, taught and made one people before any more rafters are cut.

options.text: Let the roof be seen from afar.

modifiers.name: Architects of Governance
modifiers.text: Council houses and belt houses are raised in every country the Longhouse has taken in. The Haudenosaunee become builders and planners, and the league is made visible in timber and bark.

options.text: First make one people of those within.

modifiers.name: Longhouse Renewal
modifiers.text: The league turns inward. Those under the roof are fed, the young are taught and the elders heard, and the Longhouse is made one people while the world outside grows more threatening.

destiny.name: The War Road North
destiny.text: The war road is carried north into the Wendat country. Cahiague and Ossossane, the chief towns of the Wendat, are taken, and the empty seats of the Longhouse are filled with captives from the north.

conditions.text: Chose War Road of the Longhouse
Own Cahiague, or a subject owns it
Own Ossossane, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The War Roads Open
event.text: The war chiefs have spoken. The mourning wars will no longer be limited to small raids for captives. They will become campaigns of conquest. The Wendat, the Neutrals, the Petun: all who block the expansion of the Longhouse will be swept aside. Their towns will be burned, their people adopted or scattered, their hunting grounds absorbed into the vast territory of the Haudenosaunee. The war roads stretch north and west from the homeland, and warriors sharpen their weapons in the flickering firelight.

options.text: The Longhouse shall have no empty seats.

destiny.name: Beaver Wars Conquest
destiny.text: The remaining rivals are shattered. Kandoucho of the Neutral nation, Detroit and the Sandusky country are taken, and with them the western beaver grounds and the southern shore of the Great Lakes.

conditions.text: Own Waawiiyaataanong, or a subject owns it
Own Sandusky, or a subject owns it
Own Kandoucho, or a subject owns it

event.title: Masters of the Beaver Grounds
event.text:
Detroit has fallen. The Sandusky country is ours. Where once rival peoples controlled the western beaver trade, now Haudenosaunee hunters range freely across the Great Lakes watershed. The furs flow through our hands to the European traders, and every pelt that passes enriches the Confederacy.

But conquest creates its own dilemmas. We have defeated these peoples, but the empty lands profit no one. Do we wage total war, breaking the survivors so completely that resistance becomes impossible? Or do we follow the ancient way of adoption, bringing the vanquished into the Longhouse as new members of the clans, turning enemies into brothers and filling the empty places around our fires?

options.text: Break them utterly. The war road knows no mercy.

modifiers.name: War Without Mercy
modifiers.text: The Haudenosaunee wage total war against their rivals, breaking enemy resistance through relentless siege and assault. Survivors are scattered rather than adopted.

options.text: Adopt the vanquished into the Longhouse.

modifiers.name: Adopt the Vanquished
modifiers.text: Conquered peoples are brought into the Longhouse through the adoption system, their warriors joining Haudenosaunee war parties and their families replenishing the clans.

destiny.name: Empire of the Longhouse
destiny.text: The war roads are extended to Checagou and Mackinac, the farthest straits of the Great Lakes, and to Kaskaskia, the great town of the Illinois. Castles are planted along the war road to hold the interior of the continent.

conditions.text: Own Checagou, or a subject owns it
Own Munuscong, or a subject owns it
Own Kaskaskia, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Longhouse Stretches to the Horizon
event.text:
From the straits of Mackinac to the marshes of Checagou, from the Mohawk Valley to the Ohio Country, the Haudenosaunee Confederacy commands the interior of the continent. No fur moves without our permission. No army crosses our territory without our leave. The European coastal colonies look inland and see the Longhouse: vast, powerful, and seemingly eternal.

This is the apex of military power, but even at the summit there are choices. Do we remain the eternal warriors, perfecting the art of war until no force on this continent can stand against us? Or do we use our military dominance to adopt and incorporate, building an empire not of conquest alone but of assimilation: the Longhouse growing ever longer, welcoming new peoples into its embrace?

options.text: The war roads are eternal. We fight on.

modifiers.name: Eternal War Road
modifiers.text: The Haudenosaunee perfect the art of war across a continental empire, their warriors gaining experience from constant campaigning at the cost of neglecting agricultural development.

options.text: Every conquered people becomes our own.

modifiers.name: Empire of Adoption
modifiers.text: The Longhouse grows ever longer as conquered peoples are adopted into the Confederacy. Former enemies become loyal warriors, and the empire's strength lies in incorporation rather than destruction.

units.name: Night Raiders
units.text: Small bands of warriors who travel by night, striking from ambush and withdrawing before the enemy can organize resistance. Their speed and ferocity make them devastating raiders.

units.name: Forest Warriors
units.text: Experienced fighters trained in woodland combat, equally skilled with war club and musket. They fight from behind trees and in ravines, using the forest as both shield and weapon.

units.name: War Chief's Retinue
units.text: The personal following of a condoled war chief, veterans of many campaigns who have proven their courage and loyalty. They form the disciplined core of any Haudenosaunee army.

units.name: Musket Warriors
units.text: Warriors who have fully mastered European firearms while retaining traditional mobility and fieldcraft. They combine devastating firepower with the ability to vanish into the forest.

units.name: Canoe Raiders
units.text: River-borne raiding parties who travel vast distances by bark canoe, carrying supplies and weapons along waterways to strike targets far from home.

units.name: Great War Party
units.text: The armies of the Beaver Wars: a thousand warriors and more, many with Dutch muskets, who winter in the woods of the enemy's country and fall on his towns before the thaw. Like every war party they break off sooner than trade men for ground.

units.name: Warriors of the Six Nations
units.text: Warriors of all the nations in the field together under their war chiefs. They hold a line beside allied regulars and shoot better than most of them, and there are never many: the whole Confederacy counts some two thousand fighting men.

units.name: Mohawk Rangers
units.text: Mohawk warriors and provincial rangers serving side by side, as they did under William Johnson in the wars for Canada. A few hundred men, they range far ahead of an army and are feared out of proportion to their number.

buildings.name: Longhouse
buildings.text: The iconic communal dwelling of the Haudenosaunee: a bark-covered wooden structure housing an entire clan under one roof, with shared hearths, storage, and sleeping platforms.

buildings.name: Palisade Fortification
buildings.text: A triple row of sharpened stakes interlaced with bark, surrounding the village with a formidable wall. Platforms along the top hold piles of stones and jars of water for the defenders.

buildings.name: Council Fire
buildings.text: The ceremonial and political heart of the Confederacy, where sachems gather around a sacred fire that is never allowed to go out, debating matters that affect all the nations.

buildings.name: Wampum Workshop
buildings.text: A workshop where artisans drill, shape, and string shell beads into the wampum strings and belts that serve as diplomatic credentials, historical records, and units of exchange.

buildings.name: Three Sisters Garden
buildings.text: A polyculture garden where corn, beans, and squash grow together in mounds: each plant supporting the others in a system that produces more food per acre than European monoculture.

children.text: The location's raw material is Maize
The location's raw material is Legumes

buildings.name: Smith at the Castle
buildings.text: A resident smith and his forge in a Haudenosaunee town. The towns asked for one in treaty after treaty, to mend the guns, hatchets and kettles that came by trade and could not be made at home.

buildings.name: Carrying Place
buildings.text: A portage between two waters, as at Niagara or between the Mohawk River and Wood Creek. The nation that holds it carries the canoes and bales of every trader who passes.

buildings.name: Longhouse of the Good Message
buildings.text: The meeting house of the Gaiwiio, where the faithkeepers recite the code of Handsome Lake and the cycle of thanksgivings is kept through the year.

buildings.name: House of the Wampum Keeper
buildings.text: The Onondaga keep the belts of the whole league. In this house the belts are laid up, and on set days the keeper takes them out and reads each one aloud, so that every treaty and every nation taken in is remembered as it was spoken.

buildings.name: Castle on the War Road
buildings.text: A palisaded town planted in conquered country, as Teiaiagon and Ganatsekwyagon were planted on the north shore of Lake Ontario. Hunters and war parties go out from it, and it holds the road behind them.

list.name: Grand Council at Onondaga
list.text: The deliberative apex of the Confederacy. Fifty hereditary sachem titles, distributed among the Five Nations (Mohawk 9, Oneida 9, Onondaga 14, Cayuga 10, Seneca 8) met around the central fire at Onondaga whenever questions of war, peace, or league business were laid before them. The Mohawks and Senecas sat as the Elder Brothers on one side of the fire, the Oneidas and Cayugas as the Younger Brothers on the other, and the Onondagas as Firekeepers held the casting voice in case of deadlock. Consensus was required for league action; a single nation could refuse and the matter rested. The institution was codified in the Kaianere'ko:wa, the Great Law of Peace, recited from wampum at every condolence.

list.name: Clan Mother Council
list.text: The matrilineal foundation of Haudenosaunee governance. Each clan (Wolf, Bear, Turtle, Deer, Beaver, Hawk, Eel, Snipe, Heron) held its sachem titles in trust through its senior matrons. The clan mother nominated the holder of each title, presented him for confirmation, and could recall him for misconduct, cowardice, or failure to heed the women's counsel. She also held the right to raise mourning wars to replace deceased clan members, and to forbid a war her warriors proposed by withholding the moccasins, dried corn, and parched meal needed for the campaign. The institution was the hinge on which Haudenosaunee politics turned.

list.name: Wampum Record Office
list.text: The keepers of the league's binding memory. Wampum, the polished beads of whelk and quahog drilled into long strings and woven into pictorial belts, served as the legal, ritual, and diplomatic record of the Five Nations. The Hiawatha Belt recorded the founding alliance of the league; the Two Row Wampum recorded the Dutch covenant of 1613; the Covenant Chain belts recorded the English alliance after 1677. Designated faithkeepers held the wampum, recited the words bound to each belt at council, and trained their successors in the texts. Until something was wampum'd it was not done; once wampum'd, it was binding for as long as the belt survived.

list.name: Covenant Chain Protocol
list.text: The diplomatic system that bound the Confederacy to colonial powers from 1613 onward. Beginning with the Two Row Wampum (Kaswenta) negotiated with Dutch traders at Tawagonshi in 1613, the Confederacy held that its alliances with European powers were two parallel rows: Indigenous and European peoples travelling the same river in separate vessels, neither steering the other's. The Dutch chain passed to the English at New York's surrender in 1664 and was renewed at Albany in 1677 as the formal Covenant Chain, polished annually by Confederacy delegations and crown commissioners through 1755. The Mohawk Theyanoguin and later Joseph Brant walked the chain to all the colonies and enforced its terms by threat of withdrawal.

conditions.text: Any of

list.name: Mourning War Apparatus
list.text: The institutional machinery of captive-taking and adoption that sustained Haudenosaunee population through the Beaver Wars (c. 1640-1701) and the smallpox attrition of the seventeenth century. The clan mother of a deceased Haudenosaunee raised the war by laying down the dead's name on the longhouse floor; the war chiefs gathered volunteers, mounted a campaign against an external nation, and returned with captives. Some captives were ritually executed in formal blood-revenge; others were adopted in the names of the deceased, given their longhouse place and their relations, and integrated as full Haudenosaunee. By 1660 perhaps a third of the Confederacy's population was adopted rather than birth-Haudenosaunee.

list.name: False Face Society
list.text: The masked medicine fraternity that administered healing ceremony, mid-winter renewal, and the seasonal feasts of the Haudenosaunee year. Members carved their living masks from a basswood tree without felling it (the spirit of the tree consenting to the carving), then wore the masks in the longhouse to drive out illness, malign spirit, and bad medicine by the violent shaking of turtle-shell rattles and the scattering of tobacco-and-ash. The society operated alongside but distinct from the Grand Council, holding its own succession, its own initiation, and its own seasonal calendar; the Husk Faces and the Society of Faces shared this medicine economy. The clan mothers coordinated with the False Faces for sickness in the longhouse, and the faithkeepers consulted them on the calendar of feasts.
